mentions.name: Buckaroo
mentions.description: A table display library for dataframes in notebook environments that adds analytics features like histograms, summary stats, sorting, and search to every dataframe. It now supports larger-than-memory datasets via lazy polars evaluation that reads arbitrarily large files without loading the whole dataframe into memory, computes summary stats in the background in groups of columns with per-column caching, and uses a Rust polars plugin that hashes columns to enable that caching. An execution framework with multiprocessing-based timeouts recovers from crashes, timeouts, and memory exhaustion, and debugging methods can turn arbitrary groups of polars expressions into a minimal reproduction test case through a git-bisect-like process. The work will be presented at PyData Boston.
mentions.problem: Exploring large datasets in notebooks is error-prone when done manually (splitting dataframes by columns and rows), and operations on large data often crash, exhaust memory, or run for a very long time; Buckaroo automates background summary stats so they work whenever individual columns fit in memory.
mentions.source_excerpt: I have been working on Buckaroo - my table display library for dataframes in notebook environments. Buckaroo adds table and analytics features like histograms, summary stats, sorting, and search to every dataframe. Recently I have been working to make it work better with large datasets.
